items.title: The geometric intersection pairing on a closed oriented manifold
items.statement: Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth $n$-manifold and let $A^a,B^b\subseteq M$ be closed oriented embedded submanifolds with $a+b=n$. Using the oriented intersection number of [[def-oriented-intersection-number]] (whose source is the compact submanifold and whose target is the closed submanifold, first factor first), set $$\langle A,B\rangle_M:=I(A,B)=I(i_A,B)\in\mathbb Z,$$ where $i_A:A\hookrightarrow M$ is the inclusion and $I(i_A,B)$ is evaluated on any smooth map homotopic to $i_A$ and transverse to $B$; when $A$ and $B$ are transverse this is the finite signed count $\sum_{p\in A\cap B}\varepsilon(p)$ of the local signs of [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]]. For non-transverse $A,B$ the value is the common value on all such transverse representatives, by [[thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]]. With $\mathbb F_2$ coefficients the same construction with the mod 2 intersection number [[def-mod-two-intersection-number]] defines $\langle A,B\rangle_{2}\in\mathbb F_2$ without orientability of $A,B$ or $M$; there [[thm-mod-two-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]] supplies the same independence. The number depends only on the homotopy classes of the two inclusions, so replacing a factor by a homotopic submanifold, or by a homotopic embedding of the same manifold, leaves it unchanged. The factor order is part of the definition: [[thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange]] gives $\langle B,A\rangle=(-1)^{ab}\langle A,B\rangle$ and $\langle B,A\rangle_2=\langle A,B\rangle_2$. No claim is made yet that the number depends only on the homology classes of $A$ and $B$ (that descent is proved in [[lem-geometric-intersection-descends-through-oriented-cobordism-of-cycles]]), nor that every homology class has an embedded representative (see [[rem-not-every-homology-class-is-represented-by-an-embedded-submanifold-integrally]]). Countable Choice is inherited from the transverse-representative selection in [[def-countable-choice]]; the finite signed counts themselves are choice-free.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** assemble the published intersection-number interfaces; no new count is minted.

1.1 The oriented clause. Since $M$ is closed and boundaryless and $A,B$ are closed embedded submanifolds of complementary dimensions, the inclusion $i_A:A\to M$ has compact source and $B$ is a closed oriented embedded submanifold, exactly the hypotheses under which [[def-oriented-intersection-number]] defines $I(i_A,B)$: either it is the finite signed sum over $A\cap B$ when $i_A\pitchfork B$, or it is the value on a transverse homotopic representative, whose independence is [[thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]]. Writing $\langle A,B\rangle_M$ for this number introduces no new invariant. [def-oriented-intersection-number, def-local-oriented-intersection-sign, given]

1.2 The mod 2 clause. In [[def-mod-two-intersection-number]] the same construction uses the parity of the finite transverse count, which needs neither orientations nor the orientability of $M$, and [[thm-mod-two-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]] gives independence of the transverse representative, so $\langle A,B\rangle_2$ is well defined in the same way. [def-mod-two-intersection-number, thm-mod-two-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant, given]

2.1 Symmetry. [[thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange]] compares the two ordered local signs at every point of a transverse intersection and gives $I(B,A)=(-1)^{ab}I(A,B)$ and its mod 2 analogue. Emptiness of $A\cap B$ contributes $0$ in both conventions. [thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange, def-local-oriented-intersection-sign, given, algebra]

3.1 Homotopy invariance in each variable. The definition identifies $\langle A,B\rangle_M$ with the function $[i_A]\mapsto I(\cdot,B)$ on homotopy classes; exchanging the factors and applying [[thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange]] exhibits the same invariance in the second variable. Thus no choice of representative in either variable changes the number, and only the countable-choice use recorded in [[def-oriented-intersection-number]] is inherited. [def-oriented-intersection-number, thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant, thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange, def-countable-choice, given] ∎

items.title: Bordant cycles have equal intersection numbers
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth $n$-manifold and let $B^b\subseteq M$ be a closed oriented embedded submanifold. Let $A_0^a,A_1^a\subseteq M$ be closed oriented embedded submanifolds with $a+b=n$. Suppose there is a compact oriented smooth $(a+1)$-manifold $W$ with boundary $\partial W=A_1\sqcup(-A_0)$ in the outward-normal-first convention and a smooth map $F:W\to M$ whose restriction to $\partial W$ is the inclusion of $A_1$ on the first component and the inclusion of $A_0$ on the second. If $F$ is transverse to $B$ and $F|_{\partial W}$ is transverse to $B$, then $$I(A_0,B)=I(A_1,B)\qquad\text{and}\qquad I_2(A_0,B)=I_2(A_1,B).$$ Transversality can always be arranged by a small perturbation of $F$ relative to $\partial W$, so the numerical hypothesis is not a restriction: any two cycles that are oriented bordant in this sense have equal intersection numbers with every $B$. The trace is compact because $W$ is compact; dropping compactness of $W$ invalidates the conclusion ([[cor-a-null-cobordant-cycle-has-zero-intersection-with-a-disjoint-boundary]] records the same boundary phenomenon for an explicit compact trace).
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** intersect the bordism with the fibre preimage of $B$ and count the boundary of the resulting compact oriented $1$-manifold.

1.1 Apply [[thm-transverse-preimage-for-manifolds-with-boundary]] to the smooth map $F:W\to M$ from the compact manifold with boundary $W$ to the boundaryless $M$ and the closed embedded submanifold $B$: since $F$ and $F|_{\partial W}$ are transverse to $B$, the preimage $S:=F^{-1}(B)$ is a compact embedded submanifold with boundary of $W$, neat, of dimension $(a+1)-b=1$, with $\partial S=S\cap\partial W=(F|_{\partial W})^{-1}(B)=A_1\cap B\sqcup A_0\cap B$. The intersections $A_i\cap B$ are finite (compact zero-dimensional closed submanifolds), so all counts below are finite. [thm-transverse-preimage-for-manifolds-with-boundary, def-neat-submanifold-of-a-manifold-with-boundary, def-embedded-smooth-submanifold-with-boundary, given]

1.2 Orient $S$ by the kernel-first preimage convention: a tangent vector $\tau\in T_pS$ is positive exactly when $\tau$ followed by a positive normal determinant of $B$ in $M$ is positive in $TW$; equivalently $\det T_pW=\det T_pS\otimes\det(T_{F(p)}M/T_{F(p)}B)$ with the quotient ray induced by $B$ and $M$ ([[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]] fixes the same ordered ray comparison, and [[def-induced-boundary-orientation]] fixes the outward-normal-first boundary orientation). At each endpoint $p\in A_i\cap B$ the vector $\tau$ is tangent to the slice $A_i$ and points inward at the initial end $A_0$ and outward at the terminal end $A_1$; comparing the determinant rays exactly as in [[cor-a-null-cobordant-cycle-has-zero-intersection-with-a-disjoint-boundary]] step 2.1 shows that the outward boundary sign of $p\in A_1\cap B$ equals $\varepsilon_{A_1}(p)$ and that of $p\in A_0\cap B$ equals $-\varepsilon_{A_0}(p)$, where $\varepsilon_{A_i}(p)$ is the local sign of the ordered pair $(A_i,B)$ of [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]]. The computation is a determinant-line identity in the ordered factors (tangent of the slice first, quotient second) and includes the zero-dimensional cases $a=0$ or $b=0$. [def-local-oriented-intersection-sign, def-induced-boundary-orientation, cor-a-null-cobordant-cycle-has-zero-intersection-with-a-disjoint-boundary, given, algebra]

2.1 Sum the outward boundary signs of the compact oriented $1$-manifold $S$: [[lem-oriented-boundary-of-a-compact-oriented-one-manifold-has-zero-signed-count]] gives $\sum_{p\in\partial S}\varepsilon_S(p)=0$. By step 1.2 this sum is $I(A_1,B)-I(A_0,B)$, with the oriented intersection numbers of [[def-oriented-intersection-number]]; hence $I(A_1,B)=I(A_0,B)$. Reduced modulo two the same boundary count gives $I_2(A_1,B)=I_2(A_0,B)$ without any orientation hypothesis. [lem-oriented-boundary-of-a-compact-oriented-one-manifold-has-zero-signed-count, def-oriented-intersection-number, step 1.2, given]

3.1 For the perturbation clause, if $F$ is only assumed to restrict to the inclusions on $\partial W$, apply [[thm-transversality-homotopy-theorem]] to make $F$ transverse to $B$ by a homotopy relative to the closed subset $\partial W$ on which $F$ is fixed and already transverse. The boundaries $A_i$ are unchanged, so step 2.1 applies to the perturbed map and yields the same equality. Countable Choice is inherited from that supplier; the finite determinant comparisons and the boundary count add no further choice. [thm-transversality-homotopy-theorem, def-countable-choice, def-smooth-map-between-manifolds-with-boundary, step 2.1] ∎

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $M$ be a closed $R$-oriented smooth $n$-manifold ($R=\mathbb Z$, or $\mathbb F_2$ with the canonical orientation), let $Z\subseteq M$ be a closed $R$-oriented embedded submanifold of dimension $z$, and put $r=n-z$. Orient the normal bundle $

u)	o M$ be a tubular embedding of the closed disc bundle onto a closed regular neighbourhood of $Z$ ([[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]]), with zero section $\zeta:Z	o D(
u)$, and let $u_

u$ under the excision isomorphism induced by $\varphi$. Then $$\alpha\cap[M]=(i_Z)_*[Z]\in H_z(M;R),$$ equivalently the image of $\alpha$ in $H^r(M;R)$ is the Poincare dual of $(i_Z)_*[Z]$. Over $\mathbb F_2$ no orientability hypothesis on $M$ or $Z$ is needed (the canonical orientations are used throughout). This is the geometric content of Cohen's Corollary 9.3/Ionel's Theorem 139 in the library's cap conventions; it is proved here because the later DT-16 pair owns its own collapse-map form of the statement and DT-12 must not depend forward on that page.

This is the argument of the published verification of the collapse form of this statement, restated with the tubular embedding and the AT Thom interface.

u))$. Excision identifies $H^r(D(

[given, construct]

1.2 Work in the open tube $U=\varphi(\operatorname{int}D(

Compact-support duality applies to the open manifold $U$ and is natural for the open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow M$: $D_M(j_!x)=j_*D_U(x)$ ([[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]], naturality clause). Since $\alpha$ is exactly $j_!$ of the compactly supported class of $u_

2.1 Local generators of the cap on the base. Put $b:=\pi_* D_U(u_

At a point $x\in Z$ choose an oriented trivializing slice chart of the tube in the normal-first coordinates $(N,T)$ of [[def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold]] and [[prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold]]. The $\mathbb F_2$ clause uses the canonical orientations; every determinant-ray comparison is unaffected. AC is used only through the general Poincare-duality and Thom suppliers. items.title: Normal bundle of the zero locus of a transverse section
items.statement: Let $E\to M$ be a smooth real vector bundle of rank $r$ over a boundaryless smooth $n$-manifold $M$, with zero section $s_0$, and let $s:M\to E$ be a smooth section transverse to the embedded submanifold $s_0(M)\subseteq E$. Then $Z=s^{-1}(s_0(M))$ is a closed embedded submanifold of $M$ of dimension $n-r$, and the vertical part of $ds$ induces a canonical isomorphism of smooth vector bundles over $Z$ $$\nu_Z=TM|_Z/TZ\;\cong\;s^*E|_Z .$$ If $M$ is $R$-oriented and $E$ is $R$-oriented, then the orientation of $\nu_Z$ induced from $M$ and $Z$ corresponds under this isomorphism to the orientation of $s^*E|_Z$ induced by the orientations of $E$ and $Z$; over $\mathbb F_2$ this is automatic.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** identify the pullback of the normal exact sequence along $s$ with the normal sequence of the preimage.

1.1 The zero section $s_0:M\to E$ is a smooth embedding ([[prop-the-zero-section-is-a-smooth-embedding]]), so by [[def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold]] its normal bundle is the quotient $\nu_{s_0}=TE|_{s_0(M)}/T(s_0(M))$; the canonical splitting $TE|_{s_0(M)}\cong TM\oplus E$ along the zero section identifies $\nu_{s_0(M)}\cong E$ as smooth bundles over $M$ ([[thm-a-vector-bundle-quotient-by-a-subbundle-is-a-smooth-vector-bundle]], [[prop-constant-rank-kernels-and-images-of-bundle-maps-over-one-base-are-subbundles]], [[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]]). [prop-the-zero-section-is-a-smooth-embedding, def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold, given]

1.2 The section $s$ is transverse to $s_0(M)$, so [[thm-transverse-preimage-theorem]] makes $Z=s^{-1}(s_0(M))$ a closed embedded submanifold of codimension $r$, and its normal bundle is the pullback of the normal bundle of the target: $\nu_Z\cong s^*\nu_{s_0(M)}$ with the isomorphism induced by $ds$ on the normal directions ([[def-a-smooth-map-transverse-to-an-embedded-submanifold]], [[def-pullback-vector-bundle-as-a-fibre-product]], [[thm-the-pullback-fibre-product-is-a-smooth-vector-bundle]], [[def-vector-bundle-map-over-a-smooth-base-map]]). Combining with step 1.1 gives $\nu_Z\cong s^*E|_Z$. [step 1.1, thm-transverse-preimage-theorem, given]

1.3 For the orientation clause, the isomorphism of step 1.1 carries the orientation of $E$ to the normal orientation of $s_0(M)$ that is induced by the ambient $E$ and the zero-section orientation ([[prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold]]); pullback along $s$ preserves this ordered determinant-line comparison because $ds$ is an orientation-preserving isomorphism on the normal directions of a transverse preimage, and the induced orientation of $Z$ in $M$ is the one for which a positive normal basis followed by a positive tangent basis of $Z$ is positive in $M$. Over $\mathbb F_2$ both sides have their unique generators. [prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Pullback of the Thom class along a transverse section computes the Euler class
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $E\to M$ be a smooth $R$-oriented rank-$r$ numerable real vector bundle in the scope of the Thom theorem over a closed $R$-oriented smooth $n$-manifold $M$, let $s:M\to E$ be a smooth section transverse to the zero section with zero locus $Z=s^{-1}(0)$ carrying the induced orientation of [[lem-normal-bundle-of-the-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-section]], and let $u_E$ be the normalized Thom class of $E$. Choose a smooth bundle metric by [[thm-every-smooth-vector-bundle-admits-a-smooth-bundle-metric]]. Lift $u_E$ uniquely to $\widetilde u_E\in H^r(D(E),D(E)\setminus s_0(M);R)$: restriction to $(D(E),S(E))$ is an isomorphism because the punctured fibres retract radially onto their spheres. After composing $s$ with the fibre-radial diffeomorphism $v\mapsto v/\sqrt{1+|v|^2}$ onto the open unit disc bundle (which fixes $Z$ and has derivative the identity at every zero), the pair pullback $s^*(\widetilde u_E)\in H^r(M,M\setminus Z;R)$ is defined, and it equals the image of the normal Thom class $u_{\nu_Z}$ under the tubular excision isomorphism supplied by [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]] and [[thm-excision-for-singular-cohomology]]. Consequently its image in $H^r(M;R)$ is the Euler class $e(E)$ of [[def-euler-class-by-zero-section-pullback-of-the-thom-class]]: the relative pullback of the Thom class along any transverse section computes $e(E)$. The zero section defines $e(E)$ by its absolute pullback; over a nonempty base it is transverse to itself exactly in rank zero; over an empty base transversality is vacuous.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** Thom naturality in a tube of the zero section plus homotopy invariance of absolute cohomology along the affine homotopy of sections.

1.1 Bounding the section. Replace $s$ by $ho\circ s$ with $ho(v)=v/(1+|v|)$; this is smooth and lands in the open unit disc bundle $\operatorname{int}D(E)$, has the same zero locus $Z$ because $ho^{-1}(0)=\{0\}$, and $dho_0=\mathrm{id}$, so transversality of $s$ to the zero section at every point of $Z$ is unchanged ([[prop-smoothness-of-a-section-is-equivalent-to-smooth-local-components]]). Thus $s$ may be assumed to map all of $M$ into $D(E)$ and $M\setminus Z$ into $D(E)\setminus s_0(M)$. [def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support, given]

items.title: The zero locus of a transverse section represents the Euler dual
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $E	o M$ be a smooth $R$-oriented rank-$r$ real vector bundle over a closed $R$-oriented smooth $n$-manifold, with $R=\mathbb Z$ or $\mathbb F_2$. Let $s$ be a smooth section transverse to the zero section. Its zero locus $Z$ is a closed embedded submanifold of dimension $n-r$ when nonempty, and $
u_Z\cong E|_Z$. Orient its normal bundle by this isomorphism and orient $Z$ in tangent-first order. Then
$$e(E)\cap[M]=(-1)^{r(n-r)}(i_Z)_*[Z]\in H_{n-r}(M;R).$$
In particular $(i_Z)_*[Z]
e0$ is equivalent to $e(E)
e0$, and either implies $Z
e\varnothing$. When $r=n$, the Euler number $\langle e(E),[M]angle$ is the signed zero count; a nonzero count forces a zero. On a disconnected base the total count may cancel even when the zero-cycle class is nonzero. For $r
e n$, no evaluation of $e(E)$ on the $n$-dimensional fundamental class is asserted. Over $\mathbb F_2$ orientations are canonical and the sign disappears. The zero section defines the Euler class by absolute pullback, and, when $M
e\varnothing$, is transverse to itself exactly in rank zero; for $M=\varnothing$ transversality is vacuous.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** combine the normal-Thom-class duality with the identification of the pulled-back Thom class as the Euler class.

1.1 By [[lem-normal-bundle-of-the-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-section]] the zero locus $Z$ is a closed embedded $(n-r)$-submanifold with $\nu_Z\cong s^*E|_Z$, and the orientation of $\nu_Z$ induced from $M$ and $Z$ corresponds to the fibre orientation of $E$. [given]

1.2 Let $\varphi:D(\nu_Z)\to M$ be a tubular embedding and $\alpha$ the extension of the normal Thom class in $H^r(M,M\setminus Z;R)$. By [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]], $\alpha\cap[M]=(i_Z)_*[Z]$. [step 1.1, given]

2.1 By [[lem-pullback-of-the-thom-class-along-a-transverse-section]] the pullback $s^*(u_E)\in H^r(M,M\setminus Z;R)$ equals the same extension $\alpha$ and its image in $H^r(M;R)$ is $e(E)$. Since the forget-support map is compatible with the relative cap product and with cap against $[M]$ ([[def-relative-cap-product]], [[def-cap-duality-map-for-an-oriented-manifold]], [[prop-cap-product-naturality-and-projection-formula]]), $e(E)\cap[M]=\alpha\cap[M]=(i_Z)_*[Z]$. [lem-pullback-of-the-thom-class-along-a-transverse-section, def-relative-cap-product, def-cap-duality-map-for-an-oriented-manifold, prop-cap-product-naturality-and-projection-formula, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Boundary cases: for empty $Z$ both sides are zero and $e(E)\cap[M]=0$; for rank zero, $Z=M$ with the orientation sign of the supplied orientation and $e(0_M,o)\cap[M]=o\cdot[M]$ matches $(i_M)_*[M]$. The $\mathbb F_2$ clause uses the canonical orientations. AC is inherited from the Thom and duality suppliers. [def-euler-class-by-zero-section-pullback-of-the-thom-class, def-axiom-of-choice, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: The geometric intersection number is the Poincare-dual cup pairing
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth $n$-manifold and let $A^a,B^b\subseteq M$ be closed oriented embedded submanifolds with $a+b=n$. Let $[A]\in H_a(M;\mathbb Z)$, $[B]\in H_b(M;\mathbb Z)$ be the images of the fundamental classes under the inclusions and let $\mathrm{PD}[A]=D_M^{-1}([A])\in H^{b}(M;\mathbb Z)$ and $\mathrm{PD}[B]=D_M^{-1}([B])\in H^{a}(M;\mathbb Z)$ be their Poincare duals with the cap-duality map $D_M$ of [[def-cap-duality-map-for-an-oriented-manifold]]. Then $$I(A,B)=\langle \mathrm{PD}[A]\smile\mathrm{PD}[B],[M]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,$$ with the cohomology-first, front-evaluation cap and cup conventions of [[def-cap-product-with-cohomology-first]] and the Kronecker evaluation of [[def-kronecker-evaluation-pairing]]. For non-transverse $A,B$ the left side is the value of [[def-geometric-intersection-pairing-on-a-closed-oriented-manifold]] on transverse homotopic representatives and the identity holds for those representatives. Over $\mathbb F_2$ the same identity holds with no orientability hypotheses and $\mathrm{PD}[A]=D^{-1}([A]_2)$. The sign convention is fixed by the same factor order as [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]]; no separate DT cap-product sign is introduced.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** reduce both sides to the normal bundle of $A$ using the Poincare-dual of a submanifold and compute the resulting restriction, exactly as Cohen's proof of Theorem 9.4 and Ionel's Theorem 139.

1.1 Reduce to a transverse pair. If $A$ or $B$ is not transverse, both sides depend only on the homotopy classes of the inclusions: the left side by [[def-geometric-intersection-pairing-on-a-closed-oriented-manifold]], and the right side because homotopic maps induce the same homology class ([[cor-homotopic-maps-induce-the-same-map-on-singular-homology]]) and $D_M$ is an isomorphism. So assume $A\pitchfork B$; then $A\cap B$ is finite ([[def-transverse-embedded-submanifolds]], [[lem-compact-transverse-complementary-intersections-are-finite]]). [def-geometric-intersection-pairing-on-a-closed-oriented-manifold, cor-homotopic-maps-induce-the-same-map-on-singular-homology, given]

1.2 The right side caps against $D_M(\mathrm{PD}[A])=[A]$. The cap/cup adjunction $\langle x\smile y,[M]\rangle=\langle y,x\cap[M]\rangle$ follows from the chain identity $(\alpha\smile\beta)\cap z=\beta\cap(\alpha\cap z)$ ([[prop-cap-product-naturality-and-projection-formula]], [[def-cap-product-with-cohomology-first]], [[thm-cap-product-boundary-identity]]) and the definition of the Kronecker pairing, and $\mathrm{PD}[A]\cap[M]=[A]$ by [[def-cap-duality-map-for-an-oriented-manifold]] ([[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]]). Hence $\langle \mathrm{PD}[A]\smile\mathrm{PD}[B],[M]\rangle=\langle\mathrm{PD}[B],[A]\rangle$. [prop-cap-product-naturality-and-projection-formula, def-cap-product-with-cohomology-first, def-kronecker-evaluation-pairing, def-cap-duality-map-for-an-oriented-manifold, algebra]

2.1 Restrict $\mathrm{PD}[B]$ to $A$. By [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]] applied to $B\subseteq M$, $\mathrm{PD}[B]$ is the extension by zero of the normal Thom class $u_{\nu_B}$ under a tubular embedding of $\nu_B$. Since $A\pitchfork B$, the preimage of that tube is a tubular neighbourhood of $A\cap B$ in $A$ and the pullback along $i_A$ of the extension is, by [[thm-naturality-and-uniqueness-of-thom-classes]] and [[lem-normal-bundle-of-the-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-section]] (applied to the inclusion $A\hookrightarrow M$ as a transverse map to $B$), the extension in $A$ of the Thom class of the normal bundle of $A\cap B$ in $A$. The normal bundle of $A\cap B$ in $A$ is $i_A^*\nu_B$, oriented so that the normal orientation followed by the tangent orientation of $A\cap B$ gives that of $A$. [lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold, lem-normal-bundle-of-the-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-section, thm-naturality-and-uniqueness-of-thom-classes, given]

2.2 Evaluate on $[A]$: by [[prop-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-oriented-bundle-section-represents-the-euler-dual]] applied to the trivial normal directions and [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]] applied inside the closed oriented manifold $A$, the extension class caps with $[A]$ to $(i_{A\cap B})_*[A\cap B]=\sum_{p\in A\cap B}\sigma_p\,[p]$, where $\sigma_p$ is the orientation sign of the point $p$ of the finite oriented $0$-manifold $A\cap B$ induced by $M$ and $\nu_{A\cap B\subset A}$. Hence $\langle\mathrm{PD}[B],[A]\rangle=\sum_p\sigma_p$. [prop-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-oriented-bundle-section-represents-the-euler-dual, lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold, def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold, algebra]

2.3 The local sign comparison. At $p\in A\cap B$ the exact sequence $0\to T_pA\cap T_pB\to T_pA\to T_pM/T_pB\to 0$ identifies $\nu_{A\cap B\subset A}\cong\nu_B|_p$ compatibly with the splittings, and since $\dim(A\cap B)=0$ the Koszul sign relating the ordered tensor products $\det T_pM\cong\det T_pA\otimes\det T_pB$ and $\det T_pA\cong\det T_p(A\cap B)\otimes\det\nu_{A\cap B\subset A}$ is $+1$. Therefore $\sigma_p$ equals the local oriented intersection sign $\varepsilon_{(A,B)}(p)$ of [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]], which compares $T_pA\oplus T_pB$ with $T_pM$ in the order $(A,B)$; this is a determinant-ray computation with the ambient orientation fixed once. [def-local-oriented-intersection-sign, def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold, algebra]

3.1 Summing steps 1.2, 2.2 and 2.3 gives $\langle\mathrm{PD}[A]\smile\mathrm{PD}[B],[M]\rangle=\sum_p\varepsilon_{(A,B)}(p)=I(A,B)$ for transverse $A,B$, and step 1.1 extends the identity to all complementary pairs. The $\mathbb F_2$ clause repeats the argument with the canonical orientations and the mod 2 count, where the sign comparison is vacuous; the relative-lemma inputs are the mod 2 clauses of the cited statements. [def-geometric-intersection-pairing-on-a-closed-oriented-manifold, def-oriented-intersection-number, step 1.1, step 2.3, algebra] ∎

items.title: The self-intersection number of a complementary-dimensional oriented submanifold
items.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented boundaryless smooth $n$-manifold and let $A^a\subseteq M$ be a closed oriented embedded submanifold with $2a=n$ (complementary self-intersection), with normal bundle $
u_A=TM|_A/TA$ oriented by [[prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold]]. Fix a tubular embedding $\varphi:D(
u_A)	o M$ of the closed disc bundle onto a closed regular neighbourhood. A **normal push-off** of $A$ is $A_s:=\varphi(s(A))$ for a smooth section $s:A	o
u_A$ whose image lies in an open disc subbundle of sufficiently small radius that $\varphi\circ s$ is an embedding; $A_s$ is then a closed embedded submanifold isotopic to $A$. When $s$ is transverse to the zero section, define the **self-intersection number** $$A\cdot A:=I(A,A_s)\in\mathbb Z,$$ using the oriented intersection number of [[def-oriented-intersection-number]] with the first factor $A$ and second factor $A_s$ ([[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]] fixes the local signs). The value is independent of the tubular embedding, the radius and the section: two small sections are joined by the affine homotopy through small sections, which produces a smooth isotopy of push-offs in $M$, and $I(A,\cdot)$ is invariant under homotopies of the second argument ([[thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]] and [[thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange]]); different tubes are isotopic by [[prop-two-tubular-neighbourhood-germs-are-isomorphic-near-the-zero-section]]. The proof of this independence is carried out in [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]], not assumed here. With $\mathbb F_2$ coefficients the mod 2 self-intersection $A\cdot_2A\in\mathbb F_2$ is defined for any boundaryless $M$ and any closed $a$-submanifold with $2a=n$ by the same transverse push-off count with [[def-mod-two-intersection-number]], with no orientability or compactness of $M$ required; only compactness of $A$ is used. Countable Choice is inherited from the transverse-representative selection.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** define by a small normal push-off; record the invariance and defer its proof to the evaluation theorem, as [[def-oriented-intersection-number]] defers well-definedness to [[thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]].

1.1 Existence of push-offs. Since $A$ is compact, its image under the zero section lies in the open disc bundle of some radius $\varepsilon>0$, and [[cor-every-closed-embedded-submanifold-has-a-smooth-neighbourhood-retraction]] plus the tubular description of [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]] shows that for small bounded sections $s$ the map $\varphi\circ s$ is an embedding with image a closed submanifold $A_s\subseteq M$ isotopic to $A$ through $t\mapsto\varphi(ts)$, $t\in[0,1]$. The zero section is $t=0$, so whenever $A\pitchfork A_s$ the count $I(A,A_s)$ is finite by [[lem-compact-transverse-complementary-intersections-are-finite]]. [cor-every-closed-embedded-submanifold-has-a-smooth-neighbourhood-retraction, thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold, prop-the-zero-section-is-a-smooth-embedding, def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support, given]

1.2 Invariance is a theorem. The affine homotopy $(x,t)\mapsto\varphi((1-t)s_0(x)+ts_1(x))$ between two small push-offs is an isotopy of embeddings, so it is a homotopy of the second argument of $I(A,\cdot)$; by [[thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]] and [[thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange]] the value is unchanged, and different tubular embeddings give isotopic push-offs by [[prop-two-tubular-neighbourhood-germs-are-isomorphic-near-the-zero-section]]. This invariance is proved with the evaluation theorem; the definition records it as a property to be established, not as an assumption. [thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant, thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange, prop-two-tubular-neighbourhood-germs-are-isomorphic-near-the-zero-section, given]

1.3 Mod 2 and noncompact ambient. For [[def-mod-two-intersection-number]] the count is finite and independent of the representative with the same isotopy argument, and neither orientability of $M$ nor compactness of $M$ enters; the ambient only needs to be boundaryless so that the local signs and the discrete transverse intersection are defined. [def-mod-two-intersection-number, thm-mod-two-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant, given] ∎

items.title: Normal push-off zeros are the self-intersection points
items.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented boundaryless smooth $n$-manifold, $A^a\subseteq M$ a closed oriented embedded submanifold with $2a=n$, $\varphi:D(
u_A)	o M$ a tubular embedding and $s:A	o
u_A$ a small smooth section, transverse to the zero section, with push-off $A_s=\varphi(s(A))$ as in [[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]]. Then, as sets, $$A\cap A_s=\varphi(Z(s)),\qquad Z(s)=\{x\in A:s(x)=0\},$$ and the intersection is transverse at each of these points. Moreover the local oriented intersection sign of [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]] at $\varphi(x)$ equals the local zero index of $s$ at $x$: in oriented local coordinates of the tube in which $M$ is written as $T_xA\oplus
u_{A,x}$ (tangent first) and the vertical derivative of $s$ at $x$ is the square matrix $J=\partial_
u s_x$, one has $$\varepsilon_{(A,A_s)}(\varphi(x))=\operatorname{sign}\det J,$$ with $\det J$ computed in the orientations of $A$ and of $
u_A$ fixed in [[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]]. In particular the self-intersection points are precisely the transverse zeros of the push-off section, with signs as displayed.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** the tube identifies the push-off graph with a section graph, and the intersection sign is a determinant.

1.1 The sets. Because $s$ is small, $s(A)\subseteq \operatorname{int}D(\nu_A)$, and $\varphi$ is injective on the disc bundle. For $p\in A$ and $q\in A$, $\varphi(p)=\varphi(s(q))$ holds iff $p=s(q)$ as points of the total space (with $p$ viewed as the zero vector over $p$), which forces $p=q$ and $s(p)=0$. Hence $A\cap A_s=\varphi(Z(s))$; transversality of $s$ to the zero section is exactly the statement that the vertical differential is surjective at each zero, so the graph $A_s$ meets $A$ transversely there ([[prop-a-vector-bundle-section-with-surjective-vertical-differential-at-every-zero-has-a-submanifold-zero-set]], [[def-transverse-embedded-submanifolds]]). [def-tubular-neighbourhood-of-an-embedded-submanifold, thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold, prop-a-vector-bundle-section-with-surjective-vertical-differential-at-every-zero-has-a-submanifold-zero-set, given]

1.2 Local model. At $x$ choose a slice chart of the tube with domain coordinates $(u,v)\in\mathbb R^a\oplus\mathbb R^a$ in which $A=\{v=0\}$, $\varphi$ is the identity chart, and the orientation of $M$ is the ordered product of the tangent orientation of $A$ and the normal orientation of $\nu_A$ ([[prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold]]). In these coordinates $A_s$ is the graph of $J u+O(|u|^2)$ where $J=\partial_\nu s_x$. The tangent space of $A_s$ at $x$ is spanned by the vectors $e_j+\sum_k J_{kj}e_{a+k}$; the map $T_xA\oplus T_xA_s\to T_xM$ written in the ordered ambient basis has matrix $\begin{pmatrix} I_a & I_a\\ 0 & J\end{pmatrix}$, whose determinant is $\det J$ (in the complementary case $2a=n$, so the matrix is square). By [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]] the sign $\varepsilon_{(A,A_s)}(x)$ is the sign of this determinant, proving the displayed identity, including the factor order (first $A$, then $A_s$). [def-local-oriented-intersection-sign, def-differential-of-a-smooth-map, def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart, algebra]

1.3 Global statement. Adding the finitely many points of $Z(s)$ (finite because $A$ is compact and zeros of a transverse section are isolated) gives $I(A,A_s)=\sum_{x\in Z(s)}\operatorname{sign}\det\partial_\nu s_x$, which is the self-intersection number of [[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]]. Sections that are not already transverse are first perturbed relative to a neighbourhood of their zeros by [[cor-a-smooth-section-can-be-perturbed-transverse-to-the-zero-section]], which does not change the isotopy class of the push-off up to homotopy. [def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold, cor-a-smooth-section-can-be-perturbed-transverse-to-the-zero-section, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: The self-intersection number is the Euler number of the normal bundle
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $M$ be an oriented boundaryless smooth $n$-manifold, $A^a\subseteq M$ a closed oriented embedded submanifold with $2a=n$, and let $
u_A=TM|_A/TA$ carry the orientation induced by $M$ and $A$ ([[prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold]]). Then the self-intersection number of [[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]] is well defined and $$A\cdot A=\langle e(
u_A),[A]angle\in\mathbb Z,$$ where $e(
u_A)\in H^{a}(A;\mathbb Z)$ is the Euler class of [[def-euler-class-by-zero-section-pullback-of-the-thom-class]] and $[A]\in H_a(A;\mathbb Z)$ is the fundamental class. In particular the self-intersection number is independent of the tubular embedding and of the transverse push-off, and it is an invariant of the pair $(A,
u_A)$. For a rank-$r$ oriented bundle $E	o M$ with $M$ closed oriented of dimension $n=r$ and a transverse section $s$, the signed zero count equals $\langle e(E),[M]angle$; this is the form in which the theorem is applied below.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** count the zeros of the push-off section (step 1) and identify that count with the Euler number through the zero-locus duality (step 2); then discharge well-definedness.

1.1 Choose a small section $s$ transverse to the zero section and let $A_s=\varphi(s(A))$ be its push-off. By [[lem-normal-push-off-zeros-are-self-intersection-points]], $A\cap A_s=\varphi(Z(s))$ with $\varepsilon_{(A,A_s)}(\varphi(x))=\operatorname{sign}\det\partial_
u s_x$ for every $x\in Z(s)$, so $A\cdot A=I(A,A_s)=\sum_{x\in Z(s)}\operatorname{sign}\det\partial_
u s_x$. [lem-normal-push-off-zeros-are-self-intersection-points, def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold, given]

1.2 The Euler number of the section. Apply [[prop-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-oriented-bundle-section-represents-the-euler-dual]] to the bundle $
u_A	o A$ and the section $s$: with the orientation of $Z(s)$ induced by $A$ and $
u_{Z(s)}\cong s^*
u_A$, $e(
u_A)\cap[A]=(i_{Z(s)})_*[Z(s)]$. Evaluating against the fundamental class, which by [[def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold]] and the cap/evaluation compatibility [[def-kronecker-evaluation-pairing]] assigns to a zero-dimensional oriented class $\sum_x\sigma_x[x]$ the sum of its coefficients, gives $\langle e(
u_A),[A]angle=\sum_x\sigma_x$ with $\sigma_x$ the orientation sign of $x\in Z(s)$. Comparing with step 1.1, it remains to identify $\sigma_x$ with $\operatorname{sign}\det\partial_
u s_x$: the normal bundle of the zero locus in $A$ is $s^*
u_A$ oriented by [[lem-normal-bundle-of-the-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-section]], and its fibre orientation is exactly the one in which $\partial_
u s_x$ is measured in the determinant computation of [[lem-normal-push-off-zeros-are-self-intersection-points]]; hence the signs agree. [prop-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-oriented-bundle-section-represents-the-euler-dual, lem-normal-bundle-of-the-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-section, def-kronecker-evaluation-pairing, def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold, algebra]

2.1 Well-definedness. If $s'$ is another small transverse section, the affine homotopy $\varphi((1-t)s+ts')$ is an isotopy of push-offs, so $I(A,A_s)=I(A,A_{s'})$ by [[thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]] applied to the second argument via [[thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange]]; a second tubular embedding gives an isotopic family by [[prop-two-tubular-neighbourhood-germs-are-isomorphic-near-the-zero-section]]. Hence the value computed in step 1.2 depends only on $(A,
u_A)$, and the definition of $A\cdot A$ is well posed. The closed-oriented assumption on $A$ and the compactness of $A$ are used; compactness of $M$ is not. [thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant, thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange, prop-two-tubular-neighbourhood-germs-are-isomorphic-near-the-zero-section, def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

items.title: The normal bundle of the diagonal is canonically the tangent bundle
items.statement: Let $M$ be a smooth boundaryless $n$-manifold and $\Delta_M=\{(x,x):x\in M\}\subseteq M\times M$ the diagonal, embedded by [[prop-the-diagonal-is-an-embedded-submanifold]]. The difference map $$T(M\times M)|_{\Delta_M}\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (v,w)\longmapsto w-v,$$ written in the canonical splitting $T(M\times M)|_{\Delta_M}\cong TM\oplus TM$ of [[thm-canonical-tangent-and-cotangent-splittings-for-products]], has kernel $T\Delta_M$ and induces a canonical isomorphism of smooth vector bundles over $\Delta_M\cong M$ $$\nu_{\Delta_M}=T(M\times M)|_{\Delta_M}/T\Delta_M\;\longrightarrow\;TM,$$ oriented so that the normal orientation followed by the tangent orientation of $\Delta_M$ is the product orientation of $M\times M$ ([[def-product-orientation]], [[prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold]]); under this orientation convention the isomorphism is orientation-preserving when $\Delta_M$ carries the orientation transported from $M$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** compute the kernel and the quotient of the difference map in the product splitting; transport the orientation through the same determinant comparison.

1.1 The map $\Phi(v,w)=w-v$ is a smooth bundle map over the diagonal (the splitting of [[thm-canonical-tangent-and-cotangent-splittings-for-products]] is smooth by [[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]] and [[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]). At $(x,x)$, $\Phi(v,w)=0$ iff $v=w$, i.e. iff $(v,w)\in T_{(x,x)}\Delta_M$; so the kernel is exactly $T\Delta_M$ and $\Phi$ descends to an isomorphism $\nu_{\Delta_M}\to TM$ by rank-nullity. Both sides are smooth vector bundles ([[thm-a-vector-bundle-quotient-by-a-subbundle-is-a-smooth-vector-bundle]], [[prop-constant-rank-kernels-and-images-of-bundle-maps-over-one-base-are-subbundles]], [[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]]). [thm-canonical-tangent-and-cotangent-splittings-for-products, def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold, given]

1.2 Orientation. In an oriented basis $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $T_xM$ the product orientation of $T_xM\oplus T_xM$ is the class of $((e_1,0),\dots,(e_n,0),(0,e_1),\dots,(0,e_n))$. The diagonal basis $\delta_i=(e_i,e_i)$ is obtained from it by the block matrix $\begin{pmatrix} I & 0\\ I & I\end{pmatrix}$ of determinant $+1$ (compare step 1.1 of [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]]'s sibling computation), while the lifts $(0,e_j)$ of the classes $\Phi(0,e_j)=e_j$ are the second block. Hence the ordered basis $(\delta_1,\dots,\delta_n,(0,e_1),\dots,(0,e_n))$ is positive in the product orientation exactly when the $e_j$ are positive in $T_xM$: the induced normal orientation (normal first, then the tangent orientation of $\Delta_M\cong M$) is carried by $\Phi$ to the tangent orientation of $M$. This is the convention of [[prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold]] and [[def-product-orientation]]. [def-product-orientation, prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold, algebra] ∎

items.title: The diagonal self-intersection is the Euler number of the tangent bundle
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth $n$-manifold and give $M\times M$ the product orientation. Then the diagonal $\Delta_M\subseteq M\times M$, oriented by the transport of the orientation of $M$ along $x\mapsto(x,x)$, is a closed oriented embedded $n$-submanifold with $2\dim\Delta_M=\dim(M\times M)$ and $$\Delta_M\cdot\Delta_M=\langle e(TM),[M]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,$$ where $e(TM)$ is the Euler class of the tangent bundle and the self-intersection number is that of [[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]]. This is the geometric form of the evaluation of the Euler class of the tangent bundle and the bridge to the Euler characteristic in the later Euler/index pair.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** apply the self-intersection/Euler-number theorem to the diagonal using the normal-bundle identification.

1.1 The diagonal is a closed embedded submanifold of dimension $n$ with $2n=\dim(M\times M)$ ([[prop-the-diagonal-is-an-embedded-submanifold]], [[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]), and the orientation transported from $M$ makes it a closed oriented submanifold of the closed oriented manifold $M\times M$. [prop-the-diagonal-is-an-embedded-submanifold, def-product-orientation, given]

1.2 By [[lem-normal-bundle-of-the-diagonal-is-canonically-tm]] its normal bundle is canonically $TM$ with the induced orientation of [[prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold]]. Applying [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]] to $\Delta_M\subseteq M\times M$ gives $\Delta_M\cdot\Delta_M=\langle e(\nu_{\Delta_M}),[\Delta_M]\rangle=\langle e(TM),[M]\rangle$ under the identification $\Delta_M\cong M$ and the orientation-preserving isomorphism of step 1.1. [lem-normal-bundle-of-the-diagonal-is-canonically-tm, thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle, prop-a-transverse-oriented-normal-bundle-orients-an-embedded-submanifold, algebra] ∎

items.title: The mod two self-intersection is the top Stiefel-Whitney evaluation
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $M$ be a boundaryless smooth $n$-manifold (not assumed orientable) and let $A^a\subseteq M$ be a closed embedded submanifold with $2a=n$; write $
u_A$ for its normal bundle. Then the mod 2 self-intersection $A\cdot_2A\in\mathbb F_2$ of [[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]] is well defined, depends only on $(A,
u_A)$, and satisfies $$A\cdot_2A=\langle w_a(
u_A),[A]angle_2\in\mathbb F_2,$$ where $w_a(
u_A)\in H^{a}(A;\mathbb F_2)$ is the top Stiefel-Whitney class of the rank-$a$ normal bundle and $[A]\in H_a(A;\mathbb F_2)$ is the mod 2 fundamental class. More generally, for a numerable real rank-$r$ bundle $E	o S$ over a closed smooth $s$-manifold (no orientability assumed in the $\mathbb F_2$ clause) and a smooth section $s$ transverse to the zero section with finite zero locus $Z$, $\#Z\equiv\langle w_r(E),[S]angle_2\pmod 2$ and $e_2(E)\cap[S]=[Z]$ where $e_2$ is the canonical mod 2 Euler class. The integral self-intersection number requires an oriented normal bundle and is not asserted here; this proposition is the mod 2 fallback, not an integral substitute.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** repeat the integral argument in $\mathbb F_2$ coefficients, where every bundle is canonically oriented and every manifold has a mod 2 fundamental class, and identify the mod 2 Euler class with the top Stiefel-Whitney class.

1.1 Canonical mod 2 data. By [[def-r-oriented-vector-bundle-and-orientation-local-system]] every real vector bundle carries a canonical $\mathbb F_2$-orientation, so $
u_A$, $TM$ and the normal Thom class are defined over $\mathbb F_2$; the mod 2 fundamental class of the closed manifold $A$ is the $\mathbb F_2$-orientation class ([[def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold]] applied to the canonical orientation). [def-r-oriented-vector-bundle-and-orientation-local-system, given]

1.2 The zero-locus duality and the push-off count have mod 2 clauses: the $\mathbb F_2$ cases of [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]], [[lem-normal-bundle-of-the-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-section]] and [[prop-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-oriented-bundle-section-represents-the-euler-dual]] give, for a small transverse section $s$ of $
u_A	o A$, $e_2(
u_A)\cap[A]=[Z(s)]$ with $Z(s)=A\cap A_s$ under the tube ([[lem-normal-push-off-zeros-are-self-intersection-points]]); evaluating on the mod 2 fundamental class gives $A\cdot_2A=\langle e_2(
u_A),[A]angle_2$, and the isotopy argument of [[thm-mod-two-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]] makes the count independent of the push-off. [lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold, prop-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-oriented-bundle-section-represents-the-euler-dual, lem-normal-push-off-zeros-are-self-intersection-points, thm-mod-two-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant, step 1.1]

1.3 Identify the classes: [[thm-mod-two-euler-class-is-the-top-stiefel-whitney-class]] states $e_2(E)=w_r(E)$ for every numerable real rank-$r$ bundle in the Thom scope over a paracompact Hausdorff base of CW homotopy type, and a closed smooth manifold is such a base. Substituting gives the displayed formula, and the general bundle form follows from the general clause of the same proposition. Over $\mathbb Z$ the same argument requires an orientation of $
u_A$ and produces [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]]; the mod 2 statement is the fallback and no integral claim is made when $
u_A$ is nonorientable ([[prop-first-stiefel-whitney-class-classifies-orientability]] shows that orientability of $
u_A$ is exactly $w_1(
u_A)=0$). [thm-mod-two-euler-class-is-the-top-stiefel-whitney-class, prop-first-stiefel-whitney-class-classifies-orientability, def-axiom-of-choice, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: A nowhere-zero section forces the Euler data to vanish
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $E	o M$ be an $R$-oriented numerable real vector bundle of rank $r\ge1$ in the Thom scope over a closed $R$-oriented smooth $n$-manifold. If $E$ admits a nowhere-zero smooth section, then the class-level vanishing $e(E)=0$ in $H^r(M;R)$ holds by [[prop-a-nowhere-zero-section-forces-the-euler-class-to-vanish]]; on this page the following geometric consequences are added and proved. (i) For every smooth section $\sigma$ disjoint from the zero section the zero locus is empty, so $e(E)\cap[M]=0$ by bilinearity of the cap product. When $r=n$ this also gives $\langle e(E),[M]angle=0$; evaluation on $[M]$ is only asserted in that degree. (ii) If $A^a\subseteq M$ is compact boundaryless embedded with $2a=n$ and $
u_A$ admits a nowhere-zero smooth section, then $A\cdot_2A=0$ without orientation assumptions on $A$ or $
u_A$. If, in addition, $M$ and $A$ carry integral orientations and $
u_A$ has their induced tangent-first orientation, then $A\cdot A=0$ as well. Geometrically the normal field pushes $A$ off itself, so the transverse count vanishes. The converse is false: vanishing of the Euler data does not in general produce a nowhere-zero section.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** cite the Gysin-sequence vanishing and derive the numerical consequences from the zero-locus and self-intersection evaluations.

1.1 Class level. A nowhere-zero section normalizes to a section of the sphere bundle, so the sphere projection is injective on cohomology and the Gysin sequence [[thm-gysin-long-exact-sequence-of-an-oriented-sphere-bundle]] forces $e(E)=0$; this is [[prop-a-nowhere-zero-section-forces-the-euler-class-to-vanish]]. [prop-a-nowhere-zero-section-forces-the-euler-class-to-vanish, thm-gysin-long-exact-sequence-of-an-oriented-sphere-bundle, given]

1.2 Numerical consequences. A section disjoint from the zero section is vacuously transverse to it with empty zero locus, so [[prop-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-oriented-bundle-section-represents-the-euler-dual]] gives $e(E)\cap[M]=0$, and the Kronecker evaluation of the zero class is $0$; part (i) follows. For part (ii), the nowhere-zero normal field is a section $s$ of $\nu_A$ with $Z(s)=\emptyset$, and the push-off $A_s$ is disjoint from $A$; [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]] and [[prop-mod-two-self-intersection-needs-no-orientation]] give $A\cdot A=\langle e(\nu_A),[A]\rangle=0$ and $A\cdot_2A=\langle w_a(\nu_A),[A]\rangle_2=0$. No converse is asserted; the failure of the converse is the published counterexample on the AT examples companion. items.statement: This page proves zero-set and self-intersection applications of characteristic classes. Algebraic topology owns the normalized Thom class [[def-thom-class-by-fiberwise-normalization]], its existence and Thom isomorphism [[thm-thom-isomorphism-for-oriented-vector-bundles]], and the Euler class $e(E)=s_0^*j^*u_E$ [[def-thom-euler-class-of-an-oriented-vector-bundle]], [[def-euler-class-by-zero-section-pullback-of-the-thom-class]]. Its naturality and ordered Whitney product are proved in [[thm-naturality-orientation-sign-and-whitney-product-for-euler-classes]] (with standard unit orientations on rank-zero inputs); the equality of the canonical mod 2 Euler class with the top Stiefel-Whitney class is proved in [[thm-mod-two-euler-class-is-the-top-stiefel-whitney-class]]. items.title: Not every integral homology class is represented by an embedded submanifold
items.statement: The geometric pairing and the self-intersection statements of this page apply to closed oriented embedded submanifolds, not to arbitrary homology classes. Not every integral homology class of a closed oriented manifold is the image of the fundamental class of a closed oriented manifold under a continuous map. Steenrod operations give obstructions to such integral realization, as in Thom's Chapter III, Section 4 and its lens-space product example (printed pp. 59-62). With $\mathbb F_2$ coefficients every class is represented by the mod-two fundamental class of a closed manifold under a map (Thom, Theorem III.2; Cohen's remark after Theorem 9.5) ([[thm-geometric-intersection-equals-the-poincare-dual-cup-pairing]] requires the geometric representatives to exist before it can be applied). The algebraic pairing of the cup product remains the general object, defined for all classes; where the design uses the geometric model it must either supply embedded representatives or pass to the algebraic statement. Cohen's remark after Theorem 9.5 records the integral and mod-two representability caveat; the Steenrod-operation obstruction is separately sourced to Thom. Realization by a map does not assert realization by an embedding.

items.title: Self-intersection of the zero section in an oriented plane bundle
items.statement: Let $S^2\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be the unit sphere with its induced orientation and let $E$ be an oriented rank-2 real bundle over $S^2$; write $Z\subseteq E$ for the zero section, a compact closed oriented surface embedded in the boundaryless oriented $4$-manifold $E$. Then $Z\cdot Z=\langle e(E),[S^2]\rangle\in\mathbb Z$. Two cases are computed. (a) For the trivial bundle $E=S^2\times\mathbb R^2$ the constant section $x\mapsto(x,(1,0))$ is nowhere zero, so $Z$ pushes off itself disjointly and $Z\cdot Z=0$. (b) For the tangent bundle $E=TS^2$, the explicit field $X(p)=e_3-z\,p$ on $p=(x,y,z)\in S^2$ (the tangential projection of the constant field $e_3$, i.e. the gradient of the height function) is a smooth section vanishing exactly at the two poles $\pm e_3$; in the projection charts $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y,\pm\sqrt{1-x^2-y^2})$ at the two poles its linearization is $-(x\partial_x+y\partial_y)+O(|(x,y)|^2)$ at $e_3$ and $+(x\partial_x+y\partial_y)+O(|(x,y)|^2)$ at $-e_3$, both with determinant $+1$ in dimension two, so both zeros are nondegenerate of index $+1$ and the signed zero count is $2$; hence $Z\cdot Z=2$. The trivial bundle realizes $0$ and the tangent bundle realizes $2$; the general oriented rank-two bundle over $S^2$ has Euler number its clutching integer, and no such general classification is used below.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** apply the self-intersection/Euler-number theorem and compute the signed zero count of an explicit section.

1.1 The zero section of $E$ is a closed embedded surface with normal bundle $\nu_Z\cong E$ oriented by $E$'s fibres, and $Z$ is compact, so [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]] gives $Z\cdot Z=\langle e(\nu_Z),[Z]\rangle=\langle e(E),[S^2]\rangle$. [thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle, given]

1.2 Case (a): the constant unit section is smooth and nowhere zero, so by [[cor-nowhere-zero-section-forces-the-euler-class-to-vanish]] both the Euler number and the self-intersection vanish. [cor-nowhere-zero-section-forces-the-euler-class-to-vanish, step 1.1]

1.3 Case (b): $S^2$ is the regular level set $|p|^2=1$ of a smooth function ([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]]) with $T_pS^2=p^\perp$, so $X(p)=e_3-zp$ satisfies $X(p)\cdot p=z-z|p|^2=0$ and is a smooth section of $TS^2$ ([[def-tangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]], [[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]], [[prop-smoothness-of-a-section-is-equivalent-to-smooth-local-components]]). It vanishes iff $e_3=zp$, i.e. iff $p=\pm e_3$. In the two slice charts $(u,v)=(x,y)/(1-z)$ and $(u',v')=(x,y)/(1+z)$ the sphere is a graph and the expressions of $X$ in the projection charts $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y,\pm\sqrt{1-x^2-y^2})$ near the two poles follow from the chain rule: to first order they are $-(x\partial_x+y\partial_y)$ at $e_3$ and $+(x\partial_x+y\partial_y)$ at $-e_3$, whose Jacobians $-I$ and $+I$ both have determinant $+1$ in dimension two, and the chart-orientation sign cancels between source and target in the local index. Hence both zeros are nondegenerate of index $+1$ and the signed zero count is $2$; [[lem-normal-push-off-zeros-are-self-intersection-points]] and [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]] identify it with $Z\cdot Z$ and with $\langle e(TS^2),[S^2]\rangle$. items.title: The diagonal in the two-sphere has self-intersection two
items.statement: Let $S^2\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ carry its induced orientation and give $S^2\times S^2$ the product orientation. Then the diagonal $\Delta\subseteq S^2\times S^2$ is a closed oriented embedded surface with $2\dim\Delta=\dim(S^2\times S^2)$ and $$\Delta\cdot\Delta=\langle e(TS^2),[S^2]\rangle=2.$$ The value $2$ is computed from the explicit tangent field $X(p)=e_3-z\,p$, whose zeros are the two poles with local index $+1$ each; it previews the Euler characteristic $\chi(S^2)=2$ of the later Euler/index pair (not used here).
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** apply the diagonal corollary and the zero-count computation of the plane-bundle example.

1.1 $\Delta$ is closed embedded of dimension $2$ with $2\cdot2=4=\dim(S^2\times S^2)$ ([[prop-the-diagonal-is-an-embedded-submanifold]], [[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]), so [[cor-diagonal-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-tm]] gives $\Delta\cdot\Delta=\langle e(TS^2),[S^2]\rangle$. By [[lem-normal-bundle-of-the-diagonal-is-canonically-tm]] the normal identification is the canonical one and the orientation is the induced one from the product orientation ([[def-product-orientation]], [[thm-canonical-tangent-and-cotangent-splittings-for-products]]). [cor-diagonal-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-tm, lem-normal-bundle-of-the-diagonal-is-canonically-tm, def-product-orientation, given]

1.2 In the charts $(u,v)=(x,y)/(1\mp z)$ of the two poles ([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]]) the field $X(p)=e_3-zp$ of [[ex-self-intersection-of-the-zero-section-in-an-oriented-plane-bundle]] has exactly the two zeros $\pm e_3$, each of index $+1$, so the signed zero count of $TS^2$ is $2$; [[lem-normal-push-off-zeros-are-self-intersection-points]] and [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]] identify that count with $\langle e(TS^2),[S^2]\rangle$. Hence $\Delta\cdot\Delta=2$. items.title: Coordinate circles give the hyperbolic intersection form on a torus
items.statement: Let $T^2=Q\times Q$ with $Q=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ carry the product smooth structure and orientation, and let $A=Q\times\{[0]\}$, $B=\{[0]\}\times Q$ be the coordinate circles. Then $A,B$ are closed oriented embedded circles and the geometric pairing of [[def-geometric-intersection-pairing-on-a-closed-oriented-manifold]] takes the values $$\langle A,A\rangle=0,\quad \langle B,B\rangle=0,\quad \langle A,B\rangle=1,\quad \langle B,A\rangle=-1,$$ so the pairing $\langle x,y\rangle=\langle\mathrm{PD}[x]\smile\mathrm{PD}[y],[T^2]\rangle$ has, on the classes $[A],[B]$, the hyperbolic matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$ of determinant $1$; in particular it is alternating on these classes and the factor order matters. The self-intersections vanish because each coordinate circle projects to a point in the other factor, so it can be pushed off itself by translating in the other factor along a nowhere-zero normal field.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** compute one transverse signed intersection and use the nowhere-zero normal fields for the self-intersections; the cup-pairing identification is item 3.

1.1 $A$ and $B$ are embedded circles cutting out by the coordinate projections ([[def-two-dimensional-torus]], [[def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers]], [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]]), and they meet transversely in the single point $([0],[0])$ with $T_{(0,0)}A=\mathbb R\partial_x$, $T_{(0,0)}B=\mathbb R\partial_y$ and $(\partial_x,\partial_y)$ the positive product frame ([[def-product-orientation]], [[thm-canonical-tangent-and-cotangent-splittings-for-products]]); hence $\langle A,B\rangle=1$ and, by [[def-geometric-intersection-pairing-on-a-closed-oriented-manifold]] and [[thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange]] with $ab=1$, $\langle B,A\rangle=-1$. [def-geometric-intersection-pairing-on-a-closed-oriented-manifold, def-product-orientation, thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange, algebra]

1.2 For the self-intersections: the constant field $\partial_y$ restricted to $A$ is a nowhere-zero section of the normal bundle of $A$ (the normal bundle is identified with the $y$-factor along $A$), and likewise $\partial_x$ for $B$; by [[cor-nowhere-zero-section-forces-the-euler-class-to-vanish]] (or directly by translating the factor) $A$ and $B$ push off themselves disjointly, so [[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]] and [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]] give $\langle A,A\rangle=0$ and $\langle B,B\rangle=0$. [def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold, thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle, algebra]

1.3 By [[thm-geometric-intersection-equals-the-poincare-dual-cup-pairing]] the same numbers are $\langle\mathrm{PD}[x]\smile\mathrm{PD}[y],[T^2]\rangle$ evaluated on the two classes, giving the displayed matrix: the factor order contributes the minus sign in degree one, and the determinant of the matrix on the classes displayed is $1$. No nondegeneracy claim for the whole pairing on $H_1(T^2;\mathbb Z)$ is made here. [thm-geometric-intersection-equals-the-poincare-dual-cup-pairing, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

items.title: The Mobius core circle has no integral oriented self-intersection but mod two data survives
items.statement: Let $L\to S^1$ be the Mobius real line bundle over the circle, the total space of which is the open Mobius band, and let $Z\subseteq L$ be its zero section (the core circle). Then $L$ is nonorientable and $H^1(S^1;\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2$, and: (i) $Z$ admits **no integral self-intersection number**: the ambient total space and the normal bundle $\nu_Z\cong L$ are nonorientable, so neither an integral orientation of $L$ nor the orientability hypothesis of [[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]] and [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]] is available, and no consistent integral signed count can be assigned: going once around the core circle reverses the normal orientation, so there is no consistent way to sign the coincidence points; (ii) the mod 2 self-intersection is nevertheless defined and equals $$Z\cdot_2Z=\langle w_1(L),[S^1]\rangle_2=1\in\mathbb F_2,$$ because $w_1(L)\neq0$ (the orientation local system of $L$ is nontrivial, [[prop-first-stiefel-whitney-class-classifies-orientability]]) and $H^1(S^1;\mathbb F_2)$ is one-dimensional. Thus nonorientability of the normal line destroys the integral self-intersection number while the mod 2 number survives; by [[prop-mod-two-self-intersection-needs-no-orientation]] no integral substitute should be inferred.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** realize the Mobius line by a nontrivial cocycle, identify its first Stiefel-Whitney class as the nonzero element, and apply the mod 2 self-intersection formula; exhibit the integral ambiguity.

1.1 Construction. Model $L$ by the rank-one smooth bundle over $S^1$ with transition function $-1$ on the double overlap of the standard two-chart cover of the circle: the vector-bundle construction from a smooth cocycle ([[def-vector-bundle-chart-and-transition-function]], [[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]]) produces a smooth real line bundle $L$ whose orientation local system is nontrivial (the loop monodromy acts by $-1$ on the fibre orientation). The tautological line over the real projective line, pulled back along the standard identification, is the standard model ([[def-real-projective-bundle-and-tautological-line]]); its degree-one class [[def-tautological-degree-one-class-on-a-real-projective-bundle]] is nonzero and fiber-generating ([[lem-tautological-degree-one-class-is-well-defined-and-fiber-generating]], [[lem-mod-two-cohomology-ring-of-infinite-real-projective-space]] for the one-dimensional $H^1$). [given, construct]

1.2 Mod 2 value. By [[prop-first-stiefel-whitney-class-classifies-orientability]], $w_1(L)\neq0$ is exactly nonorientability of $L$, so $w_1(L)$ is the nonzero element of $H^1(S^1;\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2$ and $\langle w_1(L),[S^1]\rangle_2=1$. [[prop-mod-two-self-intersection-needs-no-orientation]], applied with $A=S^1$ in the nonorientable total space $L$ (the mod 2 statement neither orients the ambient nor uses compactness of the ambient), gives $Z\cdot_2Z=\langle w_1(L),[S^1]\rangle_2=1$. [prop-mod-two-self-intersection-needs-no-orientation, prop-first-stiefel-whitney-class-classifies-orientability, thm-mod-two-euler-class-is-the-top-stiefel-whitney-class, step 1.1]

1.3 Integral ambiguity. No orientation of $L$ exists ([[def-stiefel-whitney-classes-from-the-projective-bundle-relation]] and [[prop-first-stiefel-whitney-class-classifies-orientability]]), so the integral Euler class $e(L)\in H^1(S^1;\mathbb Z)$ and the integral self-intersection number are undefined. Concretely, the monodromy around the core circle reverses the fibre orientation, so a zero of a section can be signed only relative to a local trivialization and no consistent global choice of signs exists: the signed count is well defined only up to an overall sign, not as an integer, while the parity of the zero count is $1$ in every trivialization. This is the hypothesis test that integral self-intersection needs an oriented normal bundle, and it is why [[prop-mod-two-self-intersection-needs-no-orientation]] states the fallback only modulo two.
